description: Shape 0 (n=32, b=20) sits at 1.01x on cuSOLVER syevj; a sibling proved 20 matrices underfill the GPU (20/148 SMs) and per-matrix/persistent Jacobi lost to the vendor kernel. BOLD different parallelization: pack the tiny 32x32 problem so ALL 148 SMs work -- e.g. warps-per-matrix with MANY matrices resident (a fully-unrolled register-resident analytic/Jacobi 32x32 eigensolver, each warp solving one matrix, hundreds of warps concurrent) OR a closed-form/low-degree-polynomial path exploiting n=32's tiny size. The lever is filling the machine at batch=20, not out-implementing syevj per-matrix. Targets occupancy/insufficient-parallelism; residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded.

Built + exhaustively optimized the SMEM-free, sync-free, register-resident WARP-PER-MATRIX cyclic-Jacobi eigh for shape 0 (n=32, b=20). 10 trials on top of the merged CURRENT BEST cf3d49aa8. Kernel: 2-sided cyclic Jacobi, round-robin ordering, lane l owns row l of A+V, n=32-specialized wjac_solve32<SW> with sweep+31-round loops UNROLLED at compile-time so every Ar/Vr index folds constant -> TRULY register-resident (166 regs, 0 local spill, confirmed ncu); diag/off-diag via masked reduction over constant-indexed Ar[k] (not Ar[partner], which forced local memory at first). In-kernel ascending sort via lane-rank + global scatter. Per-matrix residual+orth gate + cuSOLVER fallback (nbad=0/20). sweeps-to-converge = 6 (4 fails eigr 0.01; 5 marginal; 6 gives eigr 1.2e-5, 28x under gate). Optimization arc shape0: 1766us(t1 naive)->3131(t3 correctness fix)->1698(t4 sweeps12->6)->909(t5 register-resident, THE big win, fixed local-mem)->745(t6 in-kernel sort)->~560-725(t8/9 warps sweep, noisy under fleet contention). DECISIVE FINDING: warp-per-matrix LOSES to cuSOLVER at b=20. Kernel ~340us (nsys) vs cuSOLVER batched-Jacobi 105us. ncu head-to-head: cuSOLVER batch_parallel_jacobi<32,32,16> uses 16 WARPS/matrix ((20,1,1)x(32,16,1)=512 threads) -> 320 total warps, occ 25pct, 16 active warps/SM, eligible-warps 0.68, 38 regs; MY 1-warp/matrix = 20 total warps, occ 10pct (warps=8) or 1.56pct (warps=1), 6.3 warps/SM, eligible 0.24. So 20 matrices at 1 warp each CANNOT fill 148 SMs (Waves/SM 0.02) AND a single warp's Jacobi critical path is ~3x cuSOLVER's. Plus my path has ~15 torch host launches (gate+sort) vs cuSOLVER's 1 -> on this tiny shape host launch latency is ~half the wall. Routing shape-0 to warp-Jacobi: geomean 27100->30360 (+12pct REGRESSION). Per the no-regression guardrail I DISABLED the route (_WJAC_NMAX=0) in t10 -> HEAD is non-regressing (shape0 161us cuSOLVER, geomean 27077, 39/39 VALID, stream absent); the validated/gated kernel is BANKED in-code (flip _WJAC_NMAX=32 to re-enable). OPENINGS the measurements uncovered (manager to weigh): (1) THE key insight -- cuSOLVER wins by 16 WARPS/matrix (1 CTA/matrix, 512 threads, intra-block __syncthreads, NO cross-BLOCK sync). The brief's 'warp-per-matrix, no sync' UNDER-parallelized and the sibling's 'grid.sync across blocks' OVER-shot; the untried middle is a 1-CTA-per-matrix kernel with MANY warps cooperating via SMEM+__syncthreads (exactly cuSOLVER's shape) but with a FASTER inner loop -- e.g. tensor-core-assisted rotations, fewer sweeps (6 not cuSOLVER's more), or block-Jacobi. The brief said a sibling's '1-CTA/matrix Jacobi lost' but cuSOLVER's WINNING kernel IS 1-CTA/matrix, so that loss was implementation, not decomposition. (2) The ~15-launch torch tail (sort+gate) is ~half the wall on this shape; an in-kernel Frobenius residual gate (||AQ-QL||_F = ||offdiag(A_final)||_F EXACTLY, unitarily invariant) + in-kernel orth would cut it to ~2 launches -- but orth margin is only ~2.5x so needs care. (3) sweeps=5 is borderline (nbad 0-2); a per-sweep warp-ballot early-exit could shave it for easy matrices. (4) Not tried: FP16/tensor-core rotations, or fusing shape-0 into a bigger batched launch to amortize host overhead. Net: at b=20 this regime looks vendor-kernel-bound for 1-warp/matrix; the reachable win (if any) is multi-warp-per-matrix (cuSOLVER's own structure) done faster, not fewer warps.

WIN on shape 0 (n=32,b=20). Built the MULTI-WARP-per-matrix, 1-CTA-per-matrix SMEM Jacobi you specified and it BEATS cuSOLVER: shape 0 = 99us (low contention) / 143us (high fleet contention) vs cuSOLVER 161us = 1.13-1.63x. geomean 26569 (cuSOLVER-baseline ref) -> 25585 (3.7% BOARD improvement); no other shape changed (only n=32 routes). 39/39 VALID, nbad=0/20, stream absent, -O3. HEAD a4097e3f, route _eigh_mw_jacobi (_MWJAC_NMAX=32). THE WINNING STACK (4 levers, in build order): (1) 16 warps in 1 CTA (512 threads), warp w owns round-robin pair w, per round: compute rotation + COLUMN phase (cols p,q all rows) + __syncthreads + ROW phase (rows p,q all cols) + __syncthreads -- exactly cuSOLVER's launch shape, matched its 25% occupancy. First cut: kernel 430us (SLOWER than cuSOLVER 105us, barrier/MIO-bound, ncu eligible-warps 0.10 vs cuSOLVER 0.68). (2) 6 sweeps (measured floor; 4 fails eigr 0.01, 5 marginal) vs cuSOLVER ~15 = 2.5x fewer rounds. (3) THE BREAKTHROUGH -- pad SMEM row stride 32->33: the column phase's As[i*32+p] over all 32 rows ALL mapped to bank p (32-WAY BANK CONFLICT, fully serialized SMEM); padding spread them across banks -> kernel 430->59us (7x!), eligible-warps 0.10->0.91 (now BEATS cuSOLVER 0.68), occ still 24.8%==25%. This was the single biggest lever and the reason the naive multi-warp lost. (4) IN-KERNEL gate+finiteness+sort: eigen-residual via the EXACT Frobenius identity ||AQ-QL||_F=||offdiag(A_final)||_F (unitarily invariant, block-reduced over the CTA, conservative 1e-4 thresh), A/V finiteness folded into the same Bad flag, ascending sort via lane-rank+scatter -- removes ~20 torch host launches (2 gate GEMMs, 3 norms, 2 isfinite reductions, sort+gather, zeros-init). Torch tail is now just kernel + Bad>0.5 + any() sync. Shape 0 arc: 732 (naive multi-warp) -> 575 (in-kernel gate) -> 220 (bank-conflict fix) -> 143 (in-kernel finiteness) -> 99us (empty-Bad). Q orthogonality is guaranteed by construction (product of exact Givens; measured orth 1.3e-5). ncu final: kernel 59us (nsys)/61us (ncu) vs cuSOLVER 104us; eligible 0.91; 79 regs; 0 spill. Note: the EARLIER single-warp-per-matrix (trials 1-10, _eigh_warp_jacobi, _WJAC_NMAX=0) is banked DISABLED -- it LOST (20 warps underfill, 340us). OPENINGS still on the table: (a) the kernel is 94% of the wall and barrier-bound (2 __syncthreads/round x 31 x 6 = 372 barriers) -- a block-Jacobi variant doing more rotations between barriers, or cuSOLVER-style fused rounds, could cut the 59us further. (b) The ~40us residual host tail (Bad>0.5 + any() sync + kernel launch + input float().contiguous()) could shrink via a CUDA-graph capture of the whole shape-0 path. (c) tensor-core rotation apply (the column/row updates are rank-1-ish FP32) -- untested. (d) the conservative in-kernel Frobenius gate (1e-4) forced sweeps=5 to mass-fallback; a threshold tuned to the harness L1 gate might unlock sweeps=5 (another ~17% kernel cut) if the accuracy holds. (e) warps-per-CTA parametrization hit a register-launch limit at NW=16 in one refactor -- __launch_bounds__ could let a leaner variant co-reside 2 CTAs/SM (irrelevant at b=20 with 20 CTAs, but matters if batch grows). This is a real, submittable win -- recommend a leaderboard submission of a4097e3f.
